subject: Clarify data usage: training assurances and deletion playbook
messages:
From: Elaine Miller <elaine.miller@fintechcorp.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: security@fintechcorp.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 14:08:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify: do you use our customer data to train models? + retention details

Hi Aisha,

Quick question as we kick off the pilot: can you confirm whether Redwood ever uses customer content (API payloads, generated responses, uploaded files) to train or fine-tune models? Our security team flagged the wording in the public docs and they want an explicit, written assurance for our procurement file.

In particular:
- Do you train any models on customer content by default or ever without explicit opt-in?
- What telemetry/operational logs are retained and for how long (request/response logs, KV-cache telemetry, embeddings indices)?
- If we request deletion of a dataset, what is the expected timeline and does deletion purge backups and derived artifacts like embeddings?

We also need any evidence (DPA section, SOC 2 control reference, or a short one-pager) that we can attach to our vendor questionnaire. Can you point me to the exact doc or send a short summary for our legal team?

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Miller
Head of Security, FintechCorp

security@fintechcorp.com

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify: do you use our customer data to train models? + retention details

Hi Elaine —

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answer up front: Redwood does not use customer content to train or improve our public or internal models unless a customer explicitly opts in via a documented agreement. Below is a concise summary you can add to your vendor file; I've attached a one‑pager that cites the DPA and SOC 2 sections we typically reference.

Summary — Training usage & retention (hosted API):
- No default training: Customer-provided content (requests, responses, uploaded files) is never added to training corpora or used for fine-tuning unless the customer signs an explicit data‑use opt‑in.
- Operational telemetry: We retain request/response logs and runtime telemetry for operational/debugging and billing. Default retention is 30 days for full request/response logs; aggregated, non-identifiable metrics are stored longer for platform reliability analysis.
- Embeddings & derived artifacts: If embeddings are generated by the hosted API, they are stored per the customer's configuration. By default embeddings persist for 90 days unless you configure a shorter TTL or request deletion.
- Private/Dedicated options: For Dedicated and Private deployments, customers can elect to keep all data within their VPC/on-prem and manage retention. Redwood does not access content for hosted Private accounts unless explicitly granted for support.

Deletion & backups:
- Primary deletion window: Once you request deletion via the Console or API, primary copies are removed within 48 hours.
- Backups & replicas: Snapshots and backups are on a 30–60 day rotation depending on the storage tier; when deletion is requested we mark data for purge and it is removed from backups during the next cycle (guaranteed purge within 60 days for hosted accounts).
- Derived artifacts: We remove direct derived artifacts (embeddings, indexes) associated with deleted primary content. Aggregated, anonymized telemetry used for product metrics is not reversible but does not contain customer‑identifiable content.

Evidence & links:
- DPA clause: https://redwood.company/legal/dpa/FIN-2028-0037 (attached to this thread)
- SOC 2: we can provide the SOC 2 report under NDA or via our shared secure link.
- One‑pager attached: data_handling_one_pager.pdf (short summary for procurement)

If you want, we can hop on a 20‑minute call with Vivek (security/legal) and Monica (solutions) to walk through the DPA sections your team cares about. Are you available this week?

— Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify: do you use our customer data to train models? + retention details

Hi Elaine —

Adding a few legal/security clarifications for your procurement checklist. This is intended as a summary; the DPA linked by Aisha is the controlling document.

1) Training/Modeling guarantee
- Contractual assurance: Our standard DPA prohibits Redwood from using customer content for model training or research unless the parties have a separate written data‑use opt‑in. That prohibition is explicitly called out in Section 4.2 of the DPA.

2) Logging & telemetry retention
- Audit and operational logs: Request/response logs are retained by default for 30 days. Access to full logs is restricted to our SRE and support teams on a least‑privilege basis and is audited.
- Long‑term telemetry: Aggregated, non‑PII metrics (latency histograms, token counts, error rates) are retained longer for product stability; these metrics are processed so they cannot be traced to individual customers.

3) Deletion mechanics and backups
- Deletion request: Customer-initiated deletion requests are executed within 48 hours against the primary store.
- Backups: Snapshot retention depends on the storage tier: standard (30 days) and extended‑retention tiers (60 days). We mark deleted objects for purge and they are removed on the next backup rotation; customers requiring faster purge can request an expedited deletion service (subject to contract).

4) Embeddings & derived indexes
- Embeddings generated by the hosted API are considered customer data and fall under the same deletion guarantees. When primary data is deleted, we schedule removal of the embeddings and related indexes.

5) Private/Dedicated assurances
- For Dedicated/Private installations, customer data remains inside the customer-managed environment; Redwood's control plane accesses metadata only as required for provisioning/health checks, per contract.

If you need a redlineable clause for procurement, we can extract the DPA snippet and return it with section references. Happy to provide a SOC 2 access path under an NDA.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Thanks Aisha and Vivek — this is helpful. Two narrow follow-ups from our infra team:

1) Our integration will push streaming data through a Kafka ingestion pipeline; do request/response logs or transient KV cache telemetry include payloads from streaming calls, or is that only for REST API calls?
2) If we request deletion for a set of historical documents (used to build an embedding index last quarter), will the embedding index be rebuilt automatically to exclude that data, or do we need to request index rebuilds separately? Also how do you guarantee the deletion cascades to any async mirror or export (e.g., S3 snapshots) you might hold temporarily?

We can take the SOC2 under NDA. Could you confirm an expected maximum window for backups purge (you mentioned 60 days max, is that the contractual cap for hosted accounts?)

Best,
Elaine

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Miller <elaine.miller@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 10:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify: do you use our customer data to train models? + retention details

Hi Elaine —

Great questions — answers below with the operational steps you can expect if you sign the hosted pilot.

1) Kafka / streaming payloads
- What we log: Our ingestion layer (Kafka or HTTP) forwards request payloads to the inference runtime. For operational debugging we may persist request/response pairs in full in short‑term logs (default 30 days) regardless of ingestion path. So yes, streaming payloads can appear in request logs.
- Mitigation: If you prefer zero retention of payloads, we can configure your tenant to not retain full request logs (log only headers/metadata) for the pilot. This is a per‑tenant setting and is available on hosted plans; we'll document it in the onboarding checklist.

2) Embedding indexes & rebuilds
- Deletion cascade: When you request deletion of source documents, we delete the primary documents and schedule deletion of any embeddings or indexes produced directly from them. However, automatic index rebuilds are not performed by default (we avoid destructive changes without signoff).
- Recommended flow: Submit a deletion + rebuild request via the Console or API. We'll perform the rebuild in a controlled change window and provide a verification report once the new index no longer contains deleted vectors.

3) Backups/export purge window
- Contractual cap for hosted accounts: 60 days is the guaranteed maximum for standard hosted accounts. If you purchase an expedited purge add-on in the contract, we can shorten that to 7–14 days. For Dedicated/Private customers, backup retention is controlled by the customer's storage policy.

Operational next steps I propose:
- I will attach the DPA snippet keyed to the no‑training guarantee and circulate the onboarding checklist showing "no full request logs" configuration for your pilot.
- If you want an expedited purge clause, we can add that to the pilot SOW.
- Offer: 20‑minute call tomorrow to confirm Kafka path and toggle the tenant log retention setting.

Would 11am PT tomorrow work for you?

Thanks,
Aisha
